problem_statement: Take a 2D list, which is a list containing several lists, and flatten it into a single 1D list containing all the individual elements in their original order. Given Input: 2D List: [[1, 2, 3], [4, 5], [6, 7, 8, 9]]. Expected Output: 1D List: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9].

dimensions.name: Correctness
dimensions.description: Evaluates if the algorithm's logic correctly combines all elements into a single list while maintaining their original order.
sub_criteria: The logic correctly identifies and processes each sub-list from the input 2D list.
The logic correctly extracts each individual element from a sub-list.
The logic ensures that elements are added to the new 1D list in their original sequence.

dimensions.name: Completeness
dimensions.description: Evaluates if all necessary algorithmic components, such as loops, data structures, and handling of various input scenarios, are present in the solution.
sub_criteria: An empty 1D list is created to store the flattened elements.
A mechanism is present to iterate through each sub-list in the input 2D list.
A mechanism is present to iterate through each element within a sub-list.
The algorithm correctly handles edge cases such as an empty input 2D list or 2D lists containing empty sub-lists.

dimensions.name: Clarity
dimensions.description: Evaluates how easy it is to understand the logical flow and purpose of each step in the pseudocode.
sub_criteria: Variable names and descriptions of steps are meaningful and clearly indicate their purpose.
The logical flow of the algorithm is easy to follow step-by-step.
Each reference to a value or quantity is unambiguous.

dimensions.name: Efficiency
dimensions.description: Evaluates if the algorithm avoids unnecessary operations or redundant processing of data.
sub_criteria: The algorithm processes each element from the input 2D list exactly once to add it to the new 1D list.
The algorithm avoids creating unnecessary intermediate data structures or performing redundant traversals of the data.
